subject: Re: RFI - Capacity signalization, runbook & bakeoff scope
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@cloudforge.com>

Cc: David Park <david.park@cloudforge.com>

Subject: RFI: capacity signaling & benchmarking bakeoff scope

Hi Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. As part of CloudForge's platform evaluation we need a more prescriptive runbook for your proposed bakeoff. The RFP asks for:

- A reproducible load schedule (concurrency/arrival patterns) for 1k/5k/20k qps targets.
- Tail-latency decomposition methodology (P50/P95/P99/P999 per request class).
- Warm-up and cache-priming steps for prefix/KV caches and any model-variant fallbacks.
- Failure-injection scenarios for replica drop / region failover.
- Clear pass/fail criteria tied to cost-per-inference and latency SLO.

Can you provide a single runbook + sample artifacts we can run in our lab (we prefer CSV schedules and a one-page summary)? We have a week window starting Jan 11 to run the bakeoff.

Would you be able to commit to providing the runbook and sample load files by Dec 20?

Best,
Sarah
CloudForge RFP Team

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a single canonical runbook plus the CSV schedules. High-level notes up front so you can align expectations:

1) Warm-up and cache priming: we provide a two-step priming (cold-load of representative prefix set, then ramping steady-state). Expect ~5–15 minutes for typical 8k token prefix datasets; we include a short checklist for KV syncs and model variant warm caches.

2) Load schedules: we will deliver 3 canonical schedules (steady, diurnal spike, and sawtooth burst) with annotated concurrency points for 1k/5k/20k RPS targets. CSV includes columns: timestamp, concurrent_sessions, request_mix_id.

3) Tail decomposition: our method includes request-class segmentation (short prompt, long prompt, multi-step chat) + histogram of server-stage contributions (scheduler queuing, decoder latency, network). We'll provide scripts that annotate traces with stage tags.

4) Failure injection: we will include simulated replica kill traces and region-redirect behavior with suggested rollback/fallback timeouts to measure graceful degradation.

5) Pass/fail criteria: by default we use P99 <= client SLO (e.g., 250ms) for short prompts and an economic threshold (cost-per-1k tokens) for throughput validation. We will make thresholds parameterizable.

Deliverables by Dec 20: runbook (markdown), load CSVs, a one-page summary PDF with sample plots, and an example results JSON.

We plan to run an internal verification sweep on Dec 18 and will attach the signed artifacts to the doc.

I'll loop in Ben for the artifact package and Karthik for the tail-latency scripts.

—Evelyn
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment stub: load-schedule-3m.csv (text/csv, 6 KB)
--- Attachment stub: summary-latency-throughput.pdf (application/pdf, 120 KB)

Key excerpt from runbook: 
- Step 0: environment validation (GPU type, driver, kernel, model variant id)
- Step 1: baseline warm-up (prefix priming for 15 minutes using request_mix 1)
- Step 2: execute 'steady' schedule for 30m; collect token-level traces and KV hit rates
- Step 3: execute 'sawtooth-burst' schedule with 10s micro-bursts; observe queueing growth and tail amplification
- Step 4: inject replica drop at 70% throughput and measure fallback latency and request loss
- Step 5: post-run analysis — compute P50/P95/P99/P999 and stage breakdown (scheduler, decode, io, net)

Notes: our recommended agent for load generation is wrk-ng with the redis-backed KV priming hook to mimic prefix caching.

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Sarah / team — couple clarifying points from our tail-latency methodology so your lab can reproduce results exactly: 

- Trace headers: ensure you capture epoch timestamps at scheduler ingress and decoder completion; our analysis scripts align on those two markers.
- Request classes: we include three canonical mixes: short (<=64 tokens), medium (65–512 tokens), long (>512 tokens). Each mix has a defined seed set included in the CSV.
- Prefix cache behavior: we recommend validating both cold-start (empty KV) and hot-cache (95% KV hit). Our CSVs include explicit priming rows.
- Concurrency ladder: run the ladder for 60s at each level to allow backend autoscaler to stabilize; record autoscaler decision times (if using Redwood Dedicated).

One experimental note: some GPUs exhibit increased P99 under micro-bursts due to kernel-launch overhead; we include a short script that measures kernel launch variance and correlates it to tail spikes — useful if you want to separate infra vs. model execution tails.

I'll add the trace-alignment scripts to the Drive link and push a small sample results file.

Karthik
Applied ML / Performance
